$comment: Shared twin case table for openbindings.openapi@1 §3's scalar-resolution paragraph: what a YAML scalar in an OpenAPI artifact resolves to under YAML 1.2.2 §10.3.2's core tag resolution, and which explicit tags are refused rather than resolved. Every harness executing this table renders the case as a WHOLE OpenAPI document in YAML and loads it through its own engine's SHIPPED loader; `outcome: source-refused` means that load fails. `image` is the canonical JSON rendering (object keys sorted) of the value the loaded document carries at info/x-case. Generated by corpus-lab/scripts/build-yaml-scalar-resolution-table.mjs, which re-proves every authority quote against the pinned YAML 1.2.2 bytes before emitting a single case; edit that script, not this file.

cases.name: value|17
cases.basis: YAML 1.2.2 §10.3.2, the pinned regular-expression table: matches [-+]? [0-9]+ (Base 10)

cases.name: value|017

cases.name: value|0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
cases.basis: YAML 1.2.2 §10.3.2, the pinned regular-expression table: the magnitude is inside the double domain, so the row resolves to a number and F-O1-15 does not reach it. This cell is the representable side of the boundary the next case pins. Just past what a 64-bit integer holds, which is why the incumbent Go decoder fell through to the string here

cases.name: value|0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF

F-O1-15 spans this row too: every engine keeps the source text, and the row is pinned here in BOTH directions of the boundary so no engine can decide the question by side effect. 16^256 is 2^1024, the first magnitude this row cannot hold
